resources.string: Shows when Hear It is reading notifications aloud.
Hear It reads your notifications aloud through your headphones. Everything stays on this device — no account, no cloud, no analytics.
You choose which apps may be read aloud. All apps start disabled.
Announcements follow your rules: screen and lock state, silence, do not disturb, calls and output devices.
The next eight steps set up permissions, speech, apps and outputs. You start the service explicitly at the end.

Hear It needs notification access so it can see the notifications you allow it to read. It reads only the apps you enable, never stores content outside your chosen history mode, and never sends anything off the device.

Android 12 and later ask for nearby-device (Bluetooth) permission so Hear It can see connected headphones and stop speaking when they disconnect. Without it announcements still work, but device names may be unavailable.

Announcements use the text-to-speech engine installed on this device. Hear It does not translate text or download voices; if your language is missing, install its voice data in the system text-to-speech settings.

Android may stop background apps to save power. If announcements stop while the screen is off, allow Hear It to run without battery restrictions. No app can guarantee background execution, and behaviour differs by manufacturer.
I understand that battery optimisation can interrupt announcements
Choose which apps Hear It may read aloud. Everything starts disabled, and you can change this later per app.
No apps with a launcher icon were found.
Choose which output types announcements may use. If the active output is not allowed, nothing is spoken. Phone speaker is off by default.
No Bluetooth or wired output is connected right now.
Play a short announcement through the current speech settings. The test does not create a history entry and does not use the announcement queue.
The test announcement could not be spoken. Check the speech engine and language data.
This is a test announcement from Hear It.
Review your choices, then start Hear It. Nothing runs until you press Start, and opening the app later never starts it silently.
Android 13 and later also need notification permission for the persistent “Hear It is running” notification. Without it announcements still work, but the notification stays hidden.
Allow Bluetooth access, or skip this step.
No text-to-speech engine is available on this device.
The speech engine has no voice data for your language.
Enable at least one app before starting.
Allow at least one output type before starting.
Announcements run while the service is started. The dashboard, reading controls and settings arrive in the next phases.
